newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Scattered rainfall raises Australia wheat hopes.
newsitem.headline: Scattered rainfall raises Australia wheat hopes.

text.p: Scattered rain has begun to fall in parts of the Australian state of Victoria, raising hopes for wheatgrowers after one of the driest Aprils on record.
An official with the Victorian branch of Australia's Bureau of Meteorology said that rainfall began on Thursday night, with better falls in west coast areas, he said.
But not much rain had fallen in central areas of the state, where it was needed with sowing of wheat being imminent.
Some patchy rain was expected in that area on Sunday, although it was expected to be less than five millimetres, he said
Rain had mostly fallen south of the ranges where it could be said that the weather had broken. This was not the case in the north of the state, he said.
Victoria has had its driest April since 1988, but the seven-month period beginning October was the second driest on record after 1878/79.
No rain has fallen recently in the state of New South Wales, where Sydney, has had its driest April in 101 years.
The main area of drought in Australia's eastern seaboard wheat belt extends south from Sydney.
